item.title: Banking Reform and the Federal Reserve Act
item.description: Banking Reform and the Federal Reserve Act The Banking Reform and the Federal Reserve Act of 1913 established the modern central banking system of the United States, concluding a half-century struggle over the control of the national currency and credit.

item.title: Gospel of Wealth
item.description: Gospel of Wealth The Gospel of Wealth was the celebrated social philosophy articulated by steel industrialist andrew-carnegie in 1889 regarding the moral responsibilities of extreme wealth in a modern industrial democracy.

item.title: Standard Oil Trust
item.description: Standard Oil Trust The Standard Oil Trust was the revolutionary legal and managerial instrument devised in 1882 to unify the nationwide oil refining, pipeline, and marketing empire of john-d-rockefeller-sr under a single centralized authority.

item.title: Andrew Carnegie (1835–1919)
item.description: Andrew Carnegie Andrew Carnegie (1835–1919) was the titan of the American steel industry, the foremost exponent of the gospel-of-wealth, and the most celebrated philanthropist of the English-speaking world.

item.title: Carnegie Steel Company
item.description: Carnegie Steel Company The Carnegie Steel Company was the colossal manufacturing enterprise that made the United States the world’s leading steel producer and established Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, as the industrial workshop of the world.
